name: hemorrhage-severity-sweep
title: Hemorrhage severity sweep (BioGears)
question: How do blood loss, heart rate and mean arterial pressure over 10 minutes depend on the initial rate of a right-leg hemorrhage in the BioGears StandardMale?
hypothesis: Blood lost and heart rate rise monotonically with the initial bleed rate and MAP falls monotonically with it. BioGears' baroreflex does not hold MAP within 2 mmHg of its start for any of these bleeds. Loss grows much more slowly than the commanded rate, because BioGears lowers a bleed's rate as the local pressure falls.
objective: Run biogears_hemorrhage for 600 s at initial rates 0, 50, 100, 150, 200 and 250 mL/min (RightLeg, StandardMale@0s) and compare the final vitals across the grid.

readouts.name: total-blood-volume-lost
readouts.description: BioGears' TotalBloodLost; NaN until a bleed has started (so NaN throughout the rate-0 control).

readouts.name: irreversible-state
readouts.description: BioGears reported an irreversible state; the engine is no longer advanced.

readouts.name: hemorrhage-rate
readouts.description: Initial bleed-rate setpoint sent to the engine (recorded so figures read it from the run).

units_and_time.note: BioGears' own clock; its internal solver step is 0.02 s.
The initial rate of BioGears' hemorrhage action; BioGears then scales it with the compartment pressure.

expected_behavior.name: blood-loss-rises-with-rate
expected_behavior.condition: final value strictly increasing over rates 50 to 250 mL/min, final blood volume strictly decreasing over 0 to 250

expected_behavior.name: pressure-falls-with-rate
expected_behavior.condition: final MAP strictly decreasing over 0 to 250 mL/min; every bleeding arm leaves the 2 mmHg band around its start; at 250 mL/min at least 7 mmHg below start

expected_behavior.name: loss-is-sublinear-in-rate
expected_behavior.condition: blood lost at 250 mL/min is less than 3 times that at 50 mL/min

robustness.note: BioGears is deterministic (pybiogears probe P5); one run per rate.

controls.name: rate-0
controls.hypothesis: With no bleed nothing is lost and the vitals stay at their loaded values.
controls.expected: No blood lost (the readout stays NaN); MAP and heart rate within 1 unit of their starting values; blood volume within 30 mL.

controls.name: rate-250
controls.hypothesis: The fastest bleed produces the largest loss and the deepest pressure fall, confirming the readouts respond when the effect is certainly present.
controls.expected: The largest blood loss of the sweep and the lowest MAP, at least 7 mmHg below its start.

predictions: Pilot (workspace/experiments/hemorrhage-pilot-2026-11-16, biogears_hemorrhage run directly for 600 s, BioGears 8.2.0): rates 0 / 50 / 100 / 150 / 200 / 250 mL/min lost - / 337 / 508 / 611 / 679 / 728 mL; heart rate 72.1 / 78.0 / 81.5 / 83.9 / 85.4 / 86.9 bpm; MAP 96.2 / 92.1 / 90.3 / 88.9 / 87.9 / 87.3 mmHg from 95.9; blood volume 5549 / 5220 / 5054 / 4954 / 4888 / 4840 mL from 5532. Every bleeding arm first left the 2 mmHg band at 293 / 189 / 153 / 135 / 123 s.
preregistered.thresholds_provenance: Every threshold comes from that pilot, which ran each arm of this study with the same composite and parameters; the canonical runs repeat it through the workbench.
preregistered.pilot: The pilot ran all six arms, so these criteria are regression checks on BioGears' behaviour, not blind predictions. No bleed here keeps MAP within 2 mmHg, so the criterion is that every bleed leaves the band; and the loss saturates with rate.

falsifiability: Refuted if blood loss, heart rate or the MAP fall fails to increase with the initial rate, if any bleeding arm keeps MAP within 2 mmHg of its start, if MAP at 250 mL/min is not at least 7 mmHg below its start, or if loss scales in proportion to the commanded rate (250 mL/min losing 3 or more times what 50 mL/min does).
limitations: One patient (StandardMale), one site (RightLeg) and 10 minutes.
The rate is BioGears' initial bleed rate, not a constant flow; BioGears lowers it with the compartment pressure, so the setpoint is not the delivered flow.
Thresholds trace to a deterministic pilot of the same arms, not to physiology data.
